name: Key Features of Java
overview: Java brings a JVM, a big standard library, and a garbage collector that never asks for a tip. Match each feature to the problem it solves.

sections.title: Run on different platforms
sections.content: A compatible JVM can execute the same bytecode on another platform. The standard library provides common APIs for files, networking, and threads.

sections.title: Structure your code
sections.content: Classes group state with behavior. Interfaces define a contract. That lets two implementations serve the same caller without making the caller learn both.

images.caption: Each concept solves a different problem in an object-oriented design.

sections.title: Use the runtime deliberately
sections.content: The JVM verifies bytecode and manages memory. Garbage collection reclaims unreachable objects. Threads support concurrent work, and JIT compilation can improve frequently executed paths.

keyPoints: Explain three features with an example for each. Try the same bytecode on two platforms, a reusable interface, and a task running on another thread.

interviewQA.question: Does garbage collection prevent every memory leak?
interviewQA.answer: No. An unused object can still be retained by a reachable reference.

interviewQA.question: What makes Java portable?
interviewQA.answer: Compatible JVMs understand the same class-file format, and the standard library hides many operating-system differences.
